questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary sector activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Manufacturing.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secondary sector activities involve the processing of raw materials extracted from the primary sector into finished goods. Manufacturing is a classic example of a secondary sector activity.**
 
• **Mining, quarrying, and forestry are primary sector** activities that involve the extraction of natural resources directly from the earth. These activities are important for providing the raw materials necessary for secondary sector activities.
 
• **Manufacturing **involves the** transformation of raw materials **into finished goods using various processes such as machining, welding, assembling, and packaging. This sector is crucial for economic development and job creation.
 
• **Secondary sector activities are often energy-intensive and require a significant amount of capital investment** in machinery, equipment, and infrastructure.
 
• Other examples of secondary sector activities include construction, utilities, and transportation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mining involves the extraction of minerals **and other valuable resources from the earth's crust. It is a major primary sector activity that provides raw materials for various secondary sector activities such as manufacturing and construction.
 
• **Forestry involves the cultivation, management, and harvesting of trees** and other vegetation for commercial purposes such as timber, pulp, and paper production. It is another primary sector activity that provides raw materials for various secondary sector activities.
 
• **Quarrying involves the extraction of rocks and minerals **from quarries or open-pit mines. It is a subset of mining and is primarily used for the extraction of building materials such as stone, gravel, and sand.

questions.question: What are Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chasers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares are called Chasers.**
 
• **Chasers are responsible for chasing and tagging the runners to get them out.**
 
• Runners are the players who run around the field trying to avoid being tagged by the chasers.
 
• **Active Chasers** are the players who are currently chasing the runners.
 
• **The game of KHO KHO is one of the oldest traditional tag games in India. It is a team game.**
 
• 9 players will take the field in the beginning to start the match and 3 defenders of the opposite team try to avoid being touched by the chasers.
 
• It is a high-energy game that involves running and chasing.
 
• The motive of the sitting team is to "tag" the opponents.
 
• Blockers are the players who stand in the way of the chasers to protect the runners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The origin of Kho-Kho is very difficult to trace, but many historians believe that it is a modified form of** 'Tag'/'Catch',** which in its simplest form involves chasing and touching a person.
 
• Originating in Maharashtra**, Kho-Kho** in ancient times was played on** 'raths' or chariots and was known as Rathera.**
 
• The present appearance of the game was an adoption from the time of World War I in 1914.
 
• The Deccan Gymkhana club of Pune, Maharashtra so named and baptized by the great Indian leader Lokmanya Tilak & Bhai Narorkar drafted the first-ever rules and regulations that symbolized the metamorphosis of the game soon to follow.

questions.question: ______ the then Minister of Agriculture had been a key person in bringing the new agricultural technology to India under Green Revolution
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** C Subramaniam.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Green Revolution was started in India in 1965-68.
 
• The Green Revolution is referred to as a period when Indian agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies.
 
• Indian agriculture made a transition from old and manual methods and new, innovative, and technological methods.
 
• It included the use of products like** High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds,** tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers which were either not used or used on a very limited scale.
 
• **The Indian Green Revolution was the brainchild of M.S. Swaminathan. **
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India.**
 
• This revolution led to an increase in food grain production especially in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was a part of the larger and global Green Revolution started by Norman Borlaug.
 
• **Norman Borlaug is called the Father of the Green Revolution in the world.**
 
• **Norman Borlaug was given the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970** for his contribution to saving over 1 billion people worldwide from dying of starvation.

questions.question: The council of ministers in a state are appointed on the advice of the ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Chief minister.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The council of ministers in a state is appointed on the advice of the Chief Minister.
 
• 
 
The Council of Ministers performs the following functions:

 

Formulation of Policies:

 
• The Ministers formulate the policies of the government.
 
• The Cabinet takes decisions on all major problems—public health, relief to the disabled and unemployed, prevention of plant diseases, water storage, land tenures and production, supply, and distribution of goods.
 
• When it has formulated a policy, the appropriate department carries it out.

**Appointments**:

 
• ​The Governor has the power to appoint the Advocate-General and the Members of the State Public Service Commission. The Vice-Chancellors of the State Universities and members of various Boards and Commissions are all appointed by the Governor. The **Governor cannot make these appointments at his will. He must exercise these functions on the advice of his ministers.**

**​Control over the state exchequer:**

 
• The State budget containing the estimates of income and expenditure for the ensuing year is placed by the Finance Minister before the State Legislature. The Legislature cannot take the initiative in the case of a Money Bill. Such a Bill must be recommended by the Governor and can be introduced only by a Minister. The initiative in financial matters lies with the Executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The President of India is the head of the country **and is elected by an Electoral College consisting of the elected members of both houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
 
• **The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary in India** and is appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India.
 
• **The Governor of a state is appointed by the President of India** and is responsible for the administration of the state.
 
 
• The Governor has certain powers and functions under the Constitution of India, including the power to appoint the Chief Minister and other ministers of the state government.

questions.question: GNP stands for ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a__** **____**gross national product.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​GNP - Gross National Product.__
 
• It is the total value of all the final products and services in a given period in terms of production by a country's residents.
 
• It is calculated by taking the sum of personal consumption expenditures, domestic investment, expenditure by government, net exports, and any income earned by residents from overseas investments, and deducting the income earned within the domestic economy by foreign residents.
 
• GDP is Gross Domestic Product. It is the national output produced in a country.
 
• GNP = GDP + net property income from abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• GDP is the final value of all the goods and services produced in a country in a given year.
 
• The nominal gross domestic product is the gross domestic product (GDP) evaluated at current market prices.
 
• Real GDP, on the other hand, is calculated by taking a base year as a determinant.
 
• Real GDP adjusts for price changes due to inflation/deflation.
 
• The main difference between nominal GDP and real GDP is the adjustment for inflation.

questions.question: Who among the following is related with Mohiniyattam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Kanak Rele.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam is a traditional dance form of Kerala, India, which is known for its graceful movements and expressions.**

 
 
• **Kanak Rele** is a renowned **dancer, choreographer, and scholar** who has **contributed significantly to the promotion and development of Mohiniyattam.**

 
 
• She has established the Nalanda Dance Research Centre in Mumbai, which focuses on research, training, and documentation of various Indian classical dance forms, including Mohiniyattam.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Manjit Bawa** was a famous Indian painter, while Ratan Thiyam is a well-known theatre director and playwright. Both of them are not associated with Mohiniyattam.
 
• **Shanti Dave** was a Gujarati poet and writer, who is also not related to Mohiniyattam.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informatio__**

 
• ** Manjit Bawa **was known for his vibrant and colorful paintings, which often featured animals and mythical creatures.

 
 
• **He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1984.**

• He has been honored with numerous awards, including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.
 
 
 
• **Shanti Dave **was a prominent figure in the Gujarati literary world, who wrote poetry, essays, and novels.
 
 
• She was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1977 for her book 'Saptapadi'.
 
 
 
• ** Mohiniyattam** is believed to have originated in the **16th century, **and it is primarily performed by women.
 
 
• It combines elements of dance, music, and theatre to tell stories from Hindu mythology and folklore. The dance form is characterized by slow, graceful movements, delicate hand gestures, and subtle facial expressions.

questions.question: How is the vegetation affected by construction of large dams?

options.text: The plants produce nodules to produce nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
Vegetation gives rise to oxygen under aerobic conditions.
The growth of fungus is a lot
The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The construction of large dams leads to the flooding of vast areas, which results in the submergence of vegetation and the subsequent rotting of submerged plants under anaerobic conditions.**
 
• This rotting vegetation gives rise to large **amounts of methane,** which is a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.
 
• **The loss of vegetation** due to dam construction also affects the biodiversity of the area**, leading to the displacement of wildlife and changes** in the local ecosystem.
 
• ** In some cases,** the construction of dams may also lead to the fragmentation of habitats and the **loss of connectivity between different areas, further impacting vegetation and wildlife.**
 
• **The production of nodules** by plants to produce **nitrogen-fixing bacteria **is not directly related to the construction of large dams and is not have a significant impact on dam construction on vegetation.
 
• ** While vegetation does **produce oxygen under aerobic conditions, this is** not a direct impact of dam construction on vegetation.** The submergence and rotting of vegetation under anaerobic conditions is the primary impact of dam construction on vegetation.
 
• **The growth of fungus **may be a secondary impact of the rotting of submerged vegetation, but it is not a direct impact of dam construction on vegetation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Large dams** have a significant impact on the environment, **including vegetation, wildlife, and local communities.**
 
• **The submergence of vast areas** of land and the subsequent flooding can lead to the** displacement of people and wildlife, changes in local ecosystems, and the loss of biodiversity.**
 
• **The production of methane** due to the rotting of submerged vegetation is a significant contributor to global warming and climate change.
 
• The construction of dams may also have social and economic impacts on local communities, including the loss of livelihoods and cultural heritage.

questions.question: Which project is built for hydel power production and irrigation in the Sutlej river basin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Bhakra Nangal project.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhakra Nangal project **is a multipurpose project built on the Sutlej River in the northern Indian states of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The project was built for hydel power production and irrigation purposes.
 
• The project is one of the largest and most successful hydroelectric power projects in India.
 
• The project has a total installed capacity of 1,325 MW and can irrigate over 10 million acres of land in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sutlej River**

 
 
• The Sutlej River is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• The Sutlej River is also known as** Satadree.**
 
• It is the easternmost tributary of the **Indus River**.
 
• The Bhakra Dam is built around the river Sutlej to provide irrigation and other facilities to the **states of Punjab, Rajasthan, and Haryana.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Nagarjuna project** is a multipurpose project built on the **Krishna River in Andhra Pradesh, India.** It was built for the purpose of irrigation and hydel power production.
 
• **Hirakud project** is a multipurpose project built on the **Mahanadi River in Odisha, India**. It was built for the purpose of irrigation, flood control, and hydel power production.
 
• **The Sardar Sarovar Dam** is a multipurpose project built on the** Narmada River in Gujarat, India**. It was built for the purpose of irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydel power production.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1921.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January 1921.**
 
• It was a **joint movement** by the Indian National Congress and the **All India Khilafat Committee **to protest against the British Government's actions towards the Khilafat issue and to demand Swaraj or self-rule for India.
 
• **The movement gained widespread** support and saw mass participation from all sections of society, including peasants, workers, students, and women.
 
• However, the movement was called off by Mahatma Gandhi in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident, where a group of protesters attacked and killed police officers.
 
• The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement played a significant role in India's struggle for independence and paved the way for future movements.
 
• **The non-cooperation movement was a mass movement that was launched by Gandhi in 1920.** It was a peaceful and non-violent protest against the British government in India. 
 
• People had to resign from their government jobs. People were asked to withdraw their children from government-controlled or aided schools and colleges.
 
• After a series of events including the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, Gandhiji realized that there was no prospect of getting any fair treatment at the hands of the British, so he planned to withdraw the nation's cooperation from the British Government, thus launching the Non-Cooperation Movement and thereby marring the administrative set up of the country.
 
• This movement was a great success as it got massive encouragement from millions of Indians. This movement almost shook the British authorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Non-cooperation Movement was called off by Mahatma Gandhi after the **Chauri Chaura incident in February 1922. **
 
• Lord Reading was the viceroy of India when the Chauri Chaura incident took place.
 
• **Chittaranjan Das was the President of the Gaya Session of the Indian National Congress held in 1922.**

questions.question: When governments legally obliged food producers to add extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods it is called ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**food fortification.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Food fortification is the process of adding extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods to improve their nutritional value.**
 
• This is often done by governments to address nutrient deficiencies in the population, such as adding iodine to salt to prevent iodine deficiency disorders.
 
• **Food protection** refers to measures taken to **prevent food contamination or spoilage,** such as proper storage and handling practices.
 
• **Food adulteration i**s the addition of **harmful or inferior substances to food,** often for economic gain, and is illegal.
 
• **Food packaging **refers to the materials and** methods used to contain and protect food products during storage, transportation, and sale.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primordial prevention:** It is the first level of prevention and it aims at risk factor reduction towards an entire population through a focus on social and environmental conditions. The primordial prevention measures are promoted through national policies and laws. For example, National nutritional programs, ICDS, Mid-day meal programs, etc are providing nutritional supplements to the entire population to prevent mortality and morbidity rates in nutritional problems.
 
• **Secondary prevention:** It emphasizes early disease detection and its target is healthy-appearing individuals with subclinical forms of the disease. Secondary prevention occurs in the form of screenings.
 
• **Tertiary prevention:** It targets both clinical and outcome stages of a disease. It is implemented in symptomatic patients to reduce the severity of the disease as well as any associated sequelae. Forms of tertiary prevention are commonly rehabilitation service

questions.question: Which among the following festivals is also celebrated to remember King Mahabali in Kerala?

• It is celebrated in the Malayalam month of Chingam, which usually falls in August or September.
 
• The festival is marked by various rituals and cultural activities, including the famous snake boat race, called Vallamkali.
 
• Onam is an annual **Malayali harvest festival celebrated in the state of Kerala.**
 
• It is the official festival of the state and includes a spectrum of cultural events.
 
• Onam is celebrated to honor the homecoming of a mythical demon king Mahabali.

• **Puthandu or Tamil New Year** is celebrated in the state of Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka in mid-April.

• The Fundamental Rights have been described in **Articles 12-35, Part III of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The Right to Property (Article 31) was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act (1978).
 
• By the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, it is made a normal constitutional right under Act 300A in Part XII of the Constitution.
 
• The provision of fundamental rights was borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.
 
• Fundamental rights are:
 
 
• Right to equality (Articles 14–18)
 
• Right to freedom (Articles 19–22)
 
• Right against exploitation (Articles 23–24)
 
• Right to freedom of religion (Article 25–28)
 
• Cultural and educational rights (Articles 29–30)
